key_decisions: TD-1.3/TD-1.7 plan contradiction: behavior-specs.md pinned BYTE-IDENTICAL inputs (20 clicks, 1 s spacing, 44.1 kHz) with contradictory outcomes (TD-1.3: '60 ± 1, still wins' vs TD-1.7 P0: '120 or null, never 60'). A pure function cannot satisfy both. Resolved per the build-tdd contradiction rule: the P0 mechanism note ('out-of-band winners require the in-band alias to be non-weak, else null') is the more specific, higher-priority pin — its own rationale ('weak in-band alias reads as unsure → silence') IS TD-1.3's premise ('in-band aliases have ≈0 correlation'), so TD-1.3's 'still wins' conclusion was a plan error. Implemented the mechanism, asserted null in the test with an inline plan-bug comment, and corrected both plan files in place (user-delegated judgment; flagged here for review)

D-D's illustrative lag range 'p ∈ [H·60/BPM_MAX, H·60/BPM_MIN] frames (≈123…1024 @ 48 kHz)' is dimensionally wrong — H·60/BPM omits sampleRate (it is a sample count, not a frame count); per W-8 the implementation uses p = 60·sampleRate/(BPM·HOP) frames (≈21…172 @ 44.1 kHz, ≈23…187 @ 48 kHz). Without this, a 120 BPM train (lag 43 @ 44.1k) would sit below the '123' floor and be undetectable. Corrected in context.md + phase-2 file with a dated note; same error class as Phase 1's sine3s bucket inversion — new learning doc generalizes both

MIN_ONSET_FRAMES tuned 8 → 12 under D-D's explicit tuning contract (the three thresholds 0.75/0.6/8 are adjustable while every pinned outcome holds — all re-verified): FRAME 2048 over HOP 512 is a 75 %-overlap grid, so each click's frame energy rises over TWO frames and both increments clear the 1 % floor (probe: 6 clicks → 11 onsets-above-floor, not 6). 12 = '≈ a 3 s file at 120 BPM or longer', preserving the CR §2.4 short-file rule; smallest pinned positive train yields ≈39

Parabolic period refinement (refinePeriod, clamped ±1 lag) added as an implementation detail: the true period lands between integer lags (180 BPM = 28.71 frames @ 44.1k → lag 29 = 178 BPM, off the pinned ±1 by 2). Refining to the peak vertex keeps the integer bpm exact for the battery without a finer (costlier) sub-lag search

TEMPO gained two constants beyond the nine pinned ones, documented in context.md as-built deltas: ALIAS_MIN_CORRELATION 0.5 (the TD-1.7 mechanism's 'non-weak' threshold — the pinned prose is undefined without a number; 0.5 cleanly separates the measured ≈0.02 weak-alias bleed from ≈0.9+ real aliases) and ALIAS_BAND 0.1 (the D-D confidence prose 'within 10 %' made a named constant)

Confidence = bestScore/runner with the ratio capped at 1.0 (a larger ratio carries no information beyond 'decisive'); runner = strongest score outside the alias bands (±10 % of best/2 and best·2) and the winner's own lag. TD-1.1's pinned 'confidence ≥ 0.6' holds (measured clean-train ratios ≈1.4–2.0 → cap 1.0)

NaN/Infinity guard implemented as a per-frame sum check (one Number.isFinite per frame, not per sample) — any bad sample poisons its frame sum; the entry guards (sampleRate finite > 0, channels array non-empty, per-channel finite length) cover the rest. TD-1.13 plus robustness probes (plain Array input, 100-sample blip) confirm never-throws
learnings: NEW learning doc 2026-08-24-plan-pinned-numbers-break-in-units.md: three plan-time numeric errors in one CR (bucket inversion Phase 1; lag formula missing sampleRate Phase 2; TD-1.3/TD-1.7 byte-identical Given with contradictory Then) — all invisible to per-row arithmetic, all caught at build time by test transcription. Rules: recompute UNITS of every plan-pinned number (samples×rate÷hop=frames), bounds-check Given values against their containers, cross-check rows with identical Given, and fix the plan in place (never the test)

The R-11 broken-page RED worked as documented for a third consecutive plan phase — the runner's 'mocha.run() was never reached within the timeout — test page error' signal is unambiguous; no console-verification step was needed this time because only the new module could be the cause

DSP count-threshold calibration: a plan that pins a threshold like '6 clicks < MIN_ONSET_FRAMES (8)' assumes 1 onset per transient; the actual hop/frame geometry (overlap ratio, envelope width vs hop) determines the real count. The probe that measured 11 onsets for 6 clicks (a 15-line Node script over the real pipeline) is what made the 8→12 tuning defensible instead of a guess — measure the pipeline's actual shape before pinning thresholds against it

World-review with pre-measured numbers in the task brief (14 ms / 10.6 ms worst case) produced zero performance findings and zero action items overall — the review's job reduced to validating the flagged deviations and catching the two plan-doc errors; cheaper and sharper than Phase 1's review where the model had to benchmark itself
